title: Nvidia reportedly halts AI-server shipments to Southeast Asia as chips give back part of Monday's rebound
intro: After Monday's surge on Jensen Huang's return, US chip stocks sold off on Tuesday and Wednesday on renewed doubts about AI spending payback, and a shortened post-Thanksgiving session brought only a partial recovery. Export-control compliance was the week's supply-chain story, with Nvidia reportedly telling partners to stop shipping AI servers to four Southeast Asian countries under new US licensing rules, while Taiwan suppliers, Tokyo equipment names and China's Innolight rallied against the US decline.
movers_note: From the Monday Nov 23 close to the Friday Nov 27 close the tracked total fell 2.78% to $25.91T (20 of 62 companies rose; the six Tokyo rows span Nov 20 to Nov 27), and it is up 7.17% from the Friday Nov 20 close a week earlier; Zhongji Innolight (+23.7%), Wiwynn (+21.5%), KYEC (+17.2%), Unimicron (+15.8%) and Delta Electronics (+13.6%) gained most, while BESI (−9.9%), Nvidia (−8.8%), CoreWeave (−8.6%), Micron (−8.6%) and Nebius (−8.5%) fell most.

items.headline: Nvidia reportedly halts AI-server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries
items.summary: Citing a Financial Times report, Forbes says Nvidia told manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers with its AI chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, and that Dell and Supermicro told customers there deliveries would not go out. It is unclear whether the halt is temporary; it may relate to new US export rules requiring licenses for those four countries and Brazil.
items.source_name: Forbes via Yahoo Finance (citing Financial Times)

items.headline: Memory and foundry names give back Monday's Huang-return gains
items.summary: Nvidia fell about 6% a day after its 31% surge, Micron and SK hynix each dropped roughly 10%, Arm fell 8%, and TSMC and ASML each lost more than 3%, with CoreWeave and Nebius also lower.

items.headline: AI chip selloff extends on doubts about returns from infrastructure spending
items.summary: Nvidia fell about 5% in morning trading after a 5.9% drop on Tuesday, and AMD slid about 4% after losing more than 8% the prior session, with Broadcom, TSMC and Intel also lower as investors questioned whether heavy AI build-outs will pay back.

items.headline: Chips rebound in the shortened Black Friday session but still end the week lower
items.summary: The Philadelphia Semiconductor index rose nearly 5% yet finished the holiday week down, with Micron up more than 7% while Nvidia swung from an early gain to a loss before ending only modestly higher. The Nasdaq closed up 2.3% in the early-close session that followed the Thanksgiving shutdown.

items.headline: Neoclouds and optics jump ahead of Friday's open
items.summary: Seeking Alpha reports neocloud stocks rose 5% to 8% and optical names 5% to 7% before the bell on Friday, as reports that Nvidia chip sellers are warning providers against renting capacity to Chinese firms put the group in focus; AMD gained but remained down about 11% on the week.

items.headline: Deutsche Bank says chips have overtaken oil and gas in global export value
items.summary: Semiconductor exports passed oil and gas for the first time in the first quarter of 2026 on a rolling four-quarter basis, about $1.61 trillion against $1.53 trillion, and Deutsche Bank argues Asian chip-export earnings could be recycled into US tech and data centers.
